answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a ferrous anchor: each identity binds its earnings to one hardware-backed key that must sign a fresh puzzle seeded by the epoch's public signal. Peers publish the delta between each claimed result and an independently reproduced one, so a copied answer shows a zero delta and earns nothing. One operator wanting a thousand fakes must hold a thousand distinct sealed keys and solve a thousand fresh puzzles every epoch, paying full hardware and compute cost per fake, while an honest agent signs once.
